Pressure testing labs and in-service vessel NDE in Houston: which service your search needs

Many Houston searches that reach this page ask for a laboratory test: high pressure gas testing, pressure cycling, cyclic or transient pressure testing, pressure fatigue testing or external pressure testing. Those are qualification tests that a pressure test laboratory runs on valves, connectors, hoses, wellhead parts and other components. Atlantis does not operate a test laboratory and does not run qualification pressure tests. What Atlantis does is nondestructive examination (NDE) of pressure vessels, new or in service: ultrasonic thickness and weld examination, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant and visual testing, under ASNT Level III oversight.

What do pressure cycling and high pressure gas tests involve?

A cyclic or pressure fatigue test raises and lowers pressure on a component many thousands of times to show how many cycles it survives before it leaks or cracks. A transient test applies a fast spike, such as a surge or water hammer. An external pressure test loads the part from outside, the way deep water or vacuum service does, to check collapse resistance. Gas at high pressure stores far more energy than water at the same pressure, so laboratories run gas tests in barricaded cells with remote monitoring.

Laboratories publish these capabilities in detail. Stress Engineering Services' testing brochure lists internal pressurization to 60,000 psi, external pressurization to 30,000 psi, full-scale burst and collapse tests, and resonant fatigue tests with the pipe under internal pressure. Element's Houston Cypress capability sheet lists high-pressure, high-temperature aging and rapid gas decompression tests for non-metallic seals. When a purchase order calls for a qualification test like these, a laboratory is the right supplier.

Where NDE fits around a vessel pressure test

The pressure test and the NDE answer different questions. A hydrostatic test under ASME Section VIII Division 1 (UG-99), or a pneumatic test under UG-100 where water cannot be used, shows the vessel holds pressure on the day of the test. NDE shows what is inside the steel: remaining wall, cracks at nozzle welds, laminations and pitting under deposits. On a repair or alteration under the National Board Inspection Code, the repair organization agrees the examinations and the test with the Inspector, who accepts the work. Atlantis can perform the NDE in that sequence. It does not stamp repairs and it is not the Inspector.

Conventional NDT on Houston vessels in service

  • UT thickness at each condition monitoring location, with a dual-element probe and temperature correction on hot shells, so the owner's API 510 inspector can calculate corrosion rates. See ultrasonic testing in Houston.
  • Shear-wave UT of welds where cracking or an old repair is suspected: ultrasonic weld inspection.
  • Magnetic particle testing, including wet fluorescent MT, on carbon steel nozzle and attachment welds in amine, caustic or wet sour service: magnetic particle testing in Houston.
  • Liquid penetrant testing on stainless, duplex and nickel-alloy vessels: penetrant testing in Houston.
  • Visual examination of shell, heads, skirt, supports, insulation jacketing and nameplate to the inspector's checklist.

Radiography is not on this list because Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States. When a code or the owner asks for radiographs, the owner books a licensed radiography contractor, and an Atlantis Level III can review the films.

How Houston vessel NDE providers compare

Houston buyers can choose among national inspection firms, test laboratories and smaller field companies. Mistras describes a Houston in-lab branch with 25 work bays, immersion UT, MT, PT, visual and hardness testing, and vendor surveillance; IRISNDT lists Houston, Deer Park and Beaumont among its Texas locations. Whoever you hire, ask the same questions:

  • Under which written practice are the technicians certified, and which ASNT Level III approves the procedures?
  • Is the UT calibration block the same material and thickness range as the vessel?
  • How is each reading tied to the CML or weld number on your drawing?
  • Who supplies the minimum required thickness and who decides on continued service? That is your engineer and your API 510 inspector, not the NDE contractor.
  • When is the report issued? Agree it in writing before mobilization.

How Atlantis delivers vessel NDE in Houston

Atlantis is based in Houston, so crews reach Ship Channel, Bayport and Baytown units without long travel. Procedures and reports go through Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, and readings come back beside the previous survey with coverage limits stated. For statewide programs see API 510 NDE support in Texas; for new vessels in a fabrication shop, vendor inspection in Houston; for procedures, ASNT Level III consulting.
